A while back I was running a file server using CentOS and it worked as expected with the same RAID setup. I recently decided to switch to Debian but for some reason its seeing each drive individually rather than just 1. I tried writing files to one drive and they don't get mirrored to the other automatically.

I didn't change anything about the RAID setup. Its a StarTech 4 Port PCI SATA RAID Controller Adapter Card with two 1TB WD Red's. The drives were never used outside of this setup. The only options that come up on the controller's BIOS settings page is to format, delete or rebuild the array.

I don't have a lot of experience with RAID. Any thoughts?
Help...I Have 2 drives connected to a RAID controller configured in RAID 1. Debian 8 is seeing them as 2 separate drives.
Yes many unix based systems are a bit goofy regarding hardware raid controllers. Software raid isn't uncommon at all.

Linux usually sees the individual drives and the RAID. Sometimes it's under /dev/mapper .

But as others said a software RAID or a ZFS mirror is usually better. But it can be a bit of a pain to boot from one.
Use Cent OS or OpenSuse. They support hardware raid. I just built a web server with RAID 1 using OpenSuse.
